subtype: Stage 6: Facing it in small steps [Observer]
passage:
'Same seat as last time?' Ramesh asked outside Lecture Hall 2, hand tight on his bag strap.
'Not today,' Jatin said. 'Last week I sat right next to you. On Monday, one seat away. Today I'll be in the back row.'
'The back row? That's miles.'
'It's twelve rows. You'll see my hand if you look.' Jatin held it up. 'I'll wave.'
Ramesh swallowed. 'What if my chest does the thing?'
'Then it does the thing, you breathe, and it passes. Like Monday. I was a seat away and you stayed the whole hour. That was you, not me.'
Ramesh nodded slowly and went in.
After the lecture he came out grinning. 'I only looked back twice.'
'Twice!' Jatin clapped him on the shoulder. 'Next week I'm getting coffee during the lecture.'

qa.q: How many rows back will Jatin sit today?
qa.a: Jatin will be in the back row, twelve rows back.

qa.q: How does Jatin feel when Ramesh comes out of the lecture?
qa.a: Jatin is delighted and proud of Ramesh, cheering 'Twice!' and clapping him on the shoulder.

qa.q: Why does Jatin keep moving farther away each time?
qa.a: Reducing the help step by step, and pointing out that staying the whole hour was Ramesh's own doing, lets Ramesh build confidence in himself rather than in Jatin.

qa.q: How does Ramesh seem to feel coming out of the lecture?
qa.a: He feels proud and a little surprised, pleased that he only needed to look back twice.

grounding: It shows a friend who first sits beside an anxious classmate and then moves farther back, praising the effort so confidence grows.

subtype: Stage 6: Facing it in small steps [Observer]
passage:
When Manjula signed up for the Saturday dance class, she made me promise to come. So in week one I danced too, badly, right beside her. She kept her eyes on me the whole hour, not on the teacher.
Week two, I stood at the back with my water bottle. She looked round a lot, but she finished.
Week three, I waited in the canteen downstairs. She came down flushed and said, 'I forgot you weren't there for, like, ten minutes.'
Each time I told her the same thing: 'You did that. I just stood around.' I meant it.
In week five she didn't ask me to come at all. She texted a video of the routine instead: 'Devika!! I got the turn!!'
I watched it three times. I was prouder than I expected.

qa.q: Where did Devika wait in week three?
qa.a: Devika waited in the canteen downstairs.

qa.q: What does Manjula's 'I forgot you weren't there for, like, ten minutes' suggest?
qa.a: It suggests her fear was easing and she was starting to feel safe in the class on her own.

qa.q: Which part of Devika's help built Manjula's own confidence?
qa.a: Stepping back a little each week while telling Manjula 'You did that' handed the credit to her, so she came to trust herself rather than her helper.

qa.q: How does Manjula probably feel when she sends the video in week five?
qa.a: She feels excited and proud, eager to share that she got the turn without needing Devika there.

grounding: It shows a friend going to an anxious person's class, then stepping farther back each week while praising the effort.
